;; utf8-decode-oracle.txt — what java.nio's UTF-8 decoder answers, pinned.
;;
;; GENERATED. Each row is (input bytes) (output code points), read as two data
;; by test/chez/utf8-decode-test.ss. The outputs came from real JVM Clojure
;; (the version in test/conformance/profile.edn) evaluating
;;
;;   (String. (byte-array bs) "UTF-8")
;;
;; and taking .codePoints, because a jolt string holds code points where a Java
;; string holds UTF-16 units — the one place the two models differ on purpose.
;;
;; The inputs are 2702 random byte strings of length 1..6, drawn with a bias
;; toward lead bytes and continuation bytes so malformed sequences dominate;
;; well-formed UTF-8 is the easy half and the gate's other rows cover it.
;; Regenerate only against a real JVM — never against jolt.
